notes: The thread through every line: his humanity in plain sight (hungry, tired, alone) and his divinity in how the wild beasts behave around him.
“Jesus Christ” in full at the first mention in each subject and beat; “he” after that.

Translation: the Berean Standard Bible (BSB), a modern translation in the style of the NIV and ESV that is in the public domain, so it can be quoted freely. The Douay-Rheims stays for the Latin Bible Moretto knew. NIV, ESV and NLT are copyrighted, so I won't copy their text; if you want a particular verse in one of them, paste it in from your own Bible and the app will show it with its abbreviation.
Every verse is copied from the published BSB or Douay-Rheims text and checked by script. Verses are trimmed to the phrase that matters, with an ellipsis where words are skipped.
The BSB capitalizes He and His for God; my own lines do not.
Nothing is final. Every line stays marked draft until you approve it.

subjects.title: Jesus Christ
subjects.short: Forty days without food. Jesus Christ sits alone, his chin in his hand.

more.story: He is hungry and tired, as any man would be. Yet around him the wild animals lie still.

verses.text: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor

subjects.note: The whole idea of the piece in two verses: fully a man, and crowned. Hebrews quotes Psalm 8 and applies it to Jesus.

subjects.title: The Angels
subjects.short: Two angels come down from the upper right to serve him.

more.story: Satan quoted the psalm about angels and told him to jump from the Temple. He refused. Afterward the angels came anyway.

verses.text: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.

subjects.title: The Basilisk
subjects.short: A small winged serpent, half hidden near the center. It may be a basilisk.

more.story: In the Latin Bible Moretto knew, the psalm Satan quoted goes on to put the basilisk under foot. Here it crouches low near Jesus Christ.

verses.text: Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet.

subjects.note: Psalm 90:13 is the Latin Bible's numbering (91:13 in modern Bibles). The Met does not name the creature, so the short line says “may be”.

subjects.title: The Lion
subjects.short: The lion lies at his feet, head lowered, half outside the picture.

more.story: God sent an angel to shut the lions’ mouths for Daniel. This lion needs no angel; it lies down before Jesus Christ.

verses.text: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions.
Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed

subjects.title: The Stag
subjects.short: A stag at the left stretches forward, its head lowered toward him.

more.story: The deer is not one of the dangerous ones. Christians have long seen it as the soul, thirsty for God.

verses.text: As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul longs after You, O God.
If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.

subjects.title: The Fox
subjects.short: A fox rests a few steps from the serpent.

more.story: Every animal on this hillside has a den or a nest. The one through whom they were made has nowhere to lay his head.

verses.text: Through Him all things were made
Foxes have dens… but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.

subjects.note: Both verses are from the New Testament here; the story line carries the humanity and the divinity together.

subjects.title: The Bear
subjects.short: A bear lies in the grass, head down, as quiet as the rest.

more.story: Alone in these hills, a man would fear a bear. Beside Jesus Christ it lies down as calmly as the cow in Isaiah’s vision.

verses.text: The cow will graze with the bear, their young will lie down together
He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.

subjects.title: The Missing Picture
subjects.short: Faint cherubs at the left edge, where the original canvas was cut down.

more.story: Moretto’s painting once continued past this edge, with other scenes from the life of Jesus Christ.

verses.text: There are many more things that Jesus did.

beats.title: In the Beginning
beats.short: God gives the first man rule over every living creature.

more.story: When Adam fell, that rule was broken, and the wild animals became something to fear.

verses.text: Rule over… every creature that crawls upon the earth.

beats.title: The Promise
beats.short: God tells the serpent that a son of Eve will crush its head.

more.story: Christians have long read this as the first promise of Jesus Christ.

verses.text: He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.
But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman

beats.title: Forty Years
beats.short: Israel wandered in the wilderness for forty years and failed its test.

more.story: They complained of hunger and doubted God again and again.

verses.text: Remember that these forty years the LORD your God led you all the way in the wilderness

beats.title: Forty Days
beats.short: Jesus Christ goes into the same wilderness, hungry, for forty days.

more.story: Where Israel failed, he does not. Each time Satan tempts him, he answers from Deuteronomy.

verses.text: Man does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.

beats.title: What Is Man
beats.short: He is fully a man here, hungry and alone.

more.story: Psalm 8 gave man rule over the beasts. Hebrews says the man who finally holds it was tempted just as we are.

verses.text: You made him ruler of the works of Your hands; You have placed everything under his feet
one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.

beats.title: The Angels
beats.short: Satan promised him angels if he would leap from the Temple.

more.story: He would not test God. When the temptations ended, the angels came to serve him.

verses.text: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.

beats.title: The Lion and the Serpent
beats.short: Satan quoted Psalm 91 to Jesus. He stopped just before the verse about the lion.

more.story: In the picture, the lion and the serpent are already at his feet.

verses.text: You will tread on the lion and cobra; you will trample the young lion and serpent.
I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions

beats.note: Satan quotes Psalm 91:11–12 in Matthew 4:6; verse 13 is the next line. The modern number (91) is used here.

beats.title: That You May Believe
beats.short: This canvas was cut from a larger painting of the life of Jesus Christ.

more.story: What remains shows a hungry man who is also Lord of the wild beasts.

verses.text: These are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God
